question: Dandi March, the non-violent protest organised by Mahatma Gandhi against the British salt monopoly, culminated on:
solution:
The correct answer is __**6th April 1930**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Dandi March**, also known as the Salt March, was a major non-violent protest action in India led by **Mahatma Gandhi**.
 
• It was a direct action campaign of tax resistance and nonviolent protest against the British salt monopoly.
 
• The march began on **12th March 1930** and ended on **6th April 1930**, covering a distance of approximately 240 miles from Sabarmati Ashram to the coastal village of Dandi.
 
• On **6th April 1930**, Gandhi reached the coastal village of Dandi and ceremonially violated the law by making salt from seawater.
 
• This act of defiance was a significant event in the Indian independence movement and sparked widespread acts of civil disobedience against British rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Salt March** was one of the most important events in the Indian independence movement and had a significant impact on the global struggle for freedom and civil rights.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi's philosophy of nonviolent resistance, or **Satyagraha**, inspired movements for civil rights and freedom across the world.
 
• The march demonstrated the power of mass mobilization and nonviolent protest in challenging oppressive laws and authorities.
 
• The Dandi March is commemorated every year in India as a symbol of the country's struggle for independence and the enduring legacy of Mahatma Gandhi's leadership.
